title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-noah-garcia
content:
Top-line: Aurelia Health — mid-size regional healthcare provider (50 clinics, 8 hospitals). Looks like a good fit for Redwood Dedicated or Private (compliance + predictable throughput). Key constraints: PHI security, on-prem or VPC, tight SLA for ER/triage chatbots, procurement favors multi-year contracts with predictable unit economics.

Notes to self / summary:
- Org: CIO = Priya Menon (LinkedIn ok), Head of AI/Analytics = Mark Ruiz (likely evaluation lead), PM for patient experience = Tanya Brooks.
- Current tooling: internal chatbot prototype built on vendor X (cloud-hosted), slow during peak hours, cost spikes from bursty traffic. Using provider-managed APIs, not on-prem.
- Pain: latency for clinical triage pathways (need <300ms median token latency for real-time chat), security/compliance (HIPAA), cost predictability for high-volume triage flows, and ability to roll back models during failover.
- Champion hypothesis: Mark Ruiz + Tanya Brooks combo (technical + product) — both care about latency/cost; procurement will push for private deployment + self-hosting for PHI.

Product positioning / hook ideas:
- Lead with Dedicated + Private options: "predictable throughput + HIPAA controls". Emphasize SLA and dedicated GPU pools for low variance latency.
- Cost angle: show expected token/unit costs with and without caching/prefixing; run a small eval to show 30-50% cost reduction via batching + KV caching for triage flows.
- Reliability: demo fallbacks to smaller compatible models to avoid downtime during load spikes.
- Security: highlight KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and private control plane. Offer SOC2 + HIPAA coverage details.

Account-specific data points to verify / ask in intro call:
1) What are the peak concurrent triage sessions? (estimate: 200-800 based on size)
2) Do they have existing VPC/private connectors? On-prem infra?
3) Any regulatory timeline for PHI handling changes? (deadlines that push for private)
4) Who owns procurement vs security (names + evaluation criteria)?
5) Typical RFP cadence and procurement window length (procurement lead: Karen Li?)

Outbound email drafts (A/B test 1):
Subject: Reduce triage latency and stabilize costs for Aurelia Health
Hi Mark — quick note: saw the internal triage chatbot mention in your recent talk at HealthTech Forum. At Redwood we help healthcare teams run LLM inference with predictable latency and private deployments (HIPAA-ready). For triage flows we often reduce tail latency and unit cost by combining dedicated GPU pools + KV caching — customers see >30% cost reduction and far fewer timeouts during peak.
Would you be open to a 20-min call next week to see a cost/latency model for your workload? Happy to include a short technical pre-read.
— Noah

Outbound email drafts (A/B test 2 - more technical):
Subject: 20-min: on-prem inference + KV caching for clinical triage
Hi Tanya — I’m Noah on Partnerships at Redwood. We’ve helped a couple of regional health systems move triage/chat workloads to dedicated/private deployments to meet PHI needs while improving latency and lowering per-token cost. If you can share a short sample of your triage distribution (peak sessions, avg tokens), we can run a quick model to estimate GPU needs + expected cost savings. Interested?

Cold call / meeting script bullets:
- Quick intro (20s): Redwood Inference — inference platform for predictable latency & cost across hosted/dedicated/private.
- One-sentence problem: triage chatbots slow during peaks and procurement wants private/HIPAA controls.
- Why Redwood: dedicated GPU pools + private control plane, KMS/HSM, rollouts + tracing for regressions.
- Proof points: e.g., "Customer X reduced tail latency 40% and saved 30% on token spend" (anonymized).
- Ask: "Would you be open to a short technical call to share traffic patterns? We’ll run an initial sizing + cost model."

Objection handling (cheat sheet):
- "We already have a vendor for LLM APIs": ask what problems they still have (latency, cost unpredictability, PHI). Offer a migration/PoC path that runs non-critical traffic to validate performance.
- "Security/compliance concerns": reference SOC2/HIPAA docs, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, private control plane; offer to loop in security/infra SME for technical deep dive.
- "Procurement prefers single-vendor/cloud": present Dedicated/private as multi-cloud friendly; show cost predictability + reserved capacity options. Include committed pricing examples.
- "Switching cost / migration effort": outline 6–8 week PoC plan: sample workload ingest, model selection (open model suggestions), latency/cost benchmark, integration test, rollout + fallback plan.

Quick PoC idea (6–8 weeks):
Week 0: scoping + NDA + security questionnaire
Week 1–2: traffic sample + test harness (we provide harness + run local simulation)
Week 3: run baseline (current vendor) vs Redwood Dedicated (same traffic) — measure latency/cost
Week 4: iterate on batching/quantization/caching settings for target SLOs
Week 5: security review + deployment plan for VPC or on-prem connector
Week 6–8: pilot in production route small % of triage traffic, monitor, handover docs

Metrics to capture in PoC:
- median and 95th token latency
- error rates/timeouts during peaks
- tokens/day and cost per 1M tokens (baseline vs Redwood)
- operational knobs (batch sizes, cache hit rate) and observed impact

Open questions / follow-ups for next sync:
- Confirm org chart and intro to procurement/security names (Priya? Karen Li?)
- Pull any public mentions / slides (HealthTech talk) to reference in intro email
- Prepare HIPAA + SOC2 one-pager and a sample SOW for dedicated capacity
- Create a quick cost model template (CSV) to populate after we get traffic numbers

Misc notes / internal reminders:
- Loop in Maya for enterprise pricing examples and Jordan for privacy/security Qs before the first call.
- Prepare anonymized case study for regional health system (need ops numbers from product team).
- Keep email short. Use A/B subject lines and track opens + replies.

----
Raw brainstorm fragments (keep for later):
- Offer quick "latency health check": 1h review of their existing logs to identify hot paths (ask if they can share sanitized logs)
- Consider a joint webinar with a compliance partner on "how to run HIPAA-safe LLMs"
- Partner motion: integrations team + implementation partner for on-prem installs (quote for infra team)

End of notes.
